newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan stocks zoom to tenth straight record.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan stocks zoom to tenth straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks roared ahead to record highs for the tenth consecutive session on continued foreign interest amid surging volume, traders said.
"We're still enjoying the tonic of strong foreign orders," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo. "The good news continues and so does the buying."
The market's 19-share index closed ahead 3.55 percent at 6,130.22 points as 64 million shares traded at a total value of 11 billion bolivars ($23.7 million).
Among traded issues, 31 rose, three fell and six closed flat.

In Washington, IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus praised the initial results of Venezuela's stabilization plan, calling it a "success story" that "will be a long lasting one." "Those comments helped the market," said Activalores broker Gonzalo Alonso.

Electricidad de Caracas rose 28 bolivars to close at 562.00. Among the day's other leading trades, brokers singled out Consolidada Carabobo B, up 20.00 bolivars to close at 495.00; H.L. Boulton, up 4.85 bolivars to close at 34.00; and Sudamtex A and B shares, both up 1.50 bolivars to close at 66.00.
Traders were divided as to whether the bolsa would continue its rise. Some argued there were a number of foreign orders still to be filled,others saw a bout of imminent profit-taking.
"The rise has been so far, so fast," said one.
